category: no-code scraper with a desktop task builder

free_tier.stated: Free plan, no expiry and no credit card. The pricing page and the pricing blog give a cap of 10 tasks. The help center article about MCP and API credits gives up to 20 tasks. The cap that the service enforces is unverified: behind a sign-up. Hosted lane: preset templates run in the cloud through the MCP server at 2,000 records a week on the help center and 2,000 records a month on the MCP docs page, the period being unverified. Local lane (software the user runs): 1 device, 2 concurrent local runs, unlimited pages per run, up to 50,000 exported rows a month and 10,000 rows per export, as Excel, CSV, JSON, HTML or XML. Custom tasks extract only on the user's machine, with no cloud extraction, no API access and no task scheduling
free_tier.notes: the true units are extracted records for MCP template runs and exported data rows (50,000 a month, 10,000 per export) for custom tasks; no vocabulary term names a row or a record. The MCP allowance is 2,000 records per week on the help center, the April 2026 release notes, the pricing blog and the MCP landing page, and 2,000 records per month on the MCP docs page, which states a week in its copy archived on 2026-09-13; an AI recipes repository first committed on 2026-10-21 states a monthly row quota shared by MCP and CLI template runs on Free. The help center states that the free trial credits are not displayed on the account page, so the period the service enforces is unverified: behind a sign-up

per_object_cap.stated: 10,000 data rows per export on Free; unlimited on paid plans
per_object_cap.notes: a per-export row cap, not a byte cap

retention.stated: local runs save data on the device that ran them and Free keeps the history of the last 5 local runs; cloud data retention (30, 60 or 90 days) applies to paid plans only

egress.terms: not applicable: exported files and database or Google Sheets exports

interface_detail: Hosted lane: a remote MCP server at https://mcp.octoparse.com (OAuth or an API key) runs cloud-capable preset templates and exports JSON or CSV; the AgentTools REST API at https://openapi.octoparse.com (x-api-key header) searches and runs the same templates, and the help center gives Free and Basic accounts free records for MCP/API template extraction, but whether a Free account's key is accepted by the AgentTools endpoints is unverified: behind a sign-up. The OpenAPI for tasks, cloud runs and data needs a Standard, Professional or Enterprise account, so Free has no OpenAPI access. Local lane (software the user runs): the Octoparse desktop application builds and runs tasks by point and click, and the npm CLI (Node.js 20 or newer) runs local extraction without the desktop application and takes an account and an API key; the AI recipes README states template runs via MCP and CLI share a monthly row quota on the free plan, but whether the Free plan accepts CLI local runs of custom tasks is unverified: behind a sign-up. The true interface terms are MCP and a desktop application, which the vocabulary lacks
tooling: any MCP-compatible AI client (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code) for the hosted template lane; for custom tasks, the Octoparse desktop application (Windows 10 (64-bit) or higher, macOS 10.15 or higher) or the npm package @octoparse-ai/octoparse-cli (local extraction on Windows x64, macOS or Linux x64), installed and run by the user on a rented or free machine
chaining: the MCP lane runs preset templates on Octoparse cloud nodes and hands JSON or CSV to an AI agent with no machine at all; Free custom tasks extract only on the machine running the desktop application or the CLI, which must stay on for the run, so a rented or free Windows, macOS or Linux machine is the host

binding_note: the template lane is a separate 2,000-record allowance whose period, a week or a month, the pages state differently; for custom tasks run on the user's machine, 50,000 exported rows a month is what binds, and the 10,000-row export cap and 2 concurrent local runs only shape a single job

identity_cost.detail: the Free plan needs no credit card; sign-up is by email address with a verification code, or by Google or GitHub sign-in. The 14-day trial of a paid plan asks for a payment method

reliability_note: Free runs depend on the device, network and address of the machine that runs them: IP rotation, residential proxies and automatic CAPTCHA solving are paid features, so a protected site blocks a Free run sooner

notes: Confirmed as a no-code scraper with a free plan. Free runs: no run count is stated; 2 local runs at a time, history of the last 5. Pages per run: unlimited pages per crawl, bounded instead by 10,000 rows per export and 50,000 rows a month. Export formats: Excel, CSV, JSON, HTML, XML, plus database export (MySQL, SQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle) and Google Sheets through a service account on Free. The caveat is where Free extraction runs: the only hosted lane on Free is MCP template extraction (2,000 records a week on the help center, 2,000 records a month on the MCP docs page); custom tasks run only on the user's own machine, in the desktop application on Windows or macOS. Cloud extraction starts at Standard, from USD 69 a month billed annually.
